claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 15 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 15 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To determine your eligibility, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**First, let me ask about the age of your child:**

How old is the child you're claiming Child Benefit for? Please tell me their age or age category:
- **Under 16** years old
- **16 to 19** years old  
- **20 years or older**

Also, do you have more than one child you'd like me to assess? If so, I'll check each one for you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm looking to claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 15 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. Alex is 15 years old, which means they fall into the **under 16** category. This is great news as children under 16 have automatic qualification for Child Benefit eligibility.

Let me continue with the next step in the assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check one more thing:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

This is a standard check to ensure eligibility continues. Please let me know if Alex:
- Is **not working** in paid employment, OR
- Is **working less than 24 hours per week**

Or if Alex is working 24 hours or more per week.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - they're still in school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's perfect. Alex is in school and not working, so they meet this requirement. Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about any benefits Alex might be receiving:

**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in their own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

Please let me know if Alex is receiving either of these benefits, or if they're not receiving them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex doesn't receive any of those benefits. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?**

The rules vary depending on which part of the UK you're in:
- **England**: All types of apprenticeships (Intermediate, Advanced, Higher, Degree) would make Alex ineligible
- **Scotland**: Modern Apprenticeships would make Alex ineligible
- **Wales**: Most apprenticeships make Alex ineligible, EXCEPT Foundation Apprenticeships which are approved
- **Northern Ireland**: General apprenticeships would make Alex ineligible

Please let me know:
1. Is Alex in any apprenticeship at all?
2. If yes, which part of the UK are you in, and what type of apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't started any apprenticeship - they're just doing regular schooling.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is in regular schooling and not in any apprenticeship. Let me move forward:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status to determine if you meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit.

**Can you tell me about your residency situation? Which of the following applies to you:**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the most common situation
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** (and if so, I'll need to check additional details about your work/study/resources)
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** in certain qualifying countries
5. **Something else** - Please describe your situation

Which of these best describes your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You normally live in the UK, which means you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your responsibility for Alex:

**Which of the following applies to you:**

1. **You live with Alex** - You share the same household
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - You pay at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards their care (including food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc.)
3. **You're paying maintenance** - You make maintenance payments under a court order or agreement that covers Alex's upkeep

Which of these describes your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, so you meet the responsibility requirement. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check an important question about other potential claimants:

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or could another person (like Alex's other parent) also be claiming for them?**

Please tell me:
1. **No one else is claiming** - You're the only person claiming for Alex
2. **Yes, another person is also claiming, but we agree** - You and another claimant have agreed who should claim for Alex
3. **Yes, another person is also claiming, and there's a dispute** - There's disagreement about who should claim for Alex

Which applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is claiming for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! You're the only claimant for Alex. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check where Alex is living:

**Which of the following describes Alex's current living situation:**

1. **In hospital** - Currently staying in hospital
2. **In care** - In local authority care or other institutional care
3. **Fostered** - Being looked after by a foster carer
4. **Living at home normally** - Living with you in your home

Which applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living at home normally with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living at home with you normally. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to ask one final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- **Yes** - The council is not paying for Alex's accommodation or upkeep (you're covering these costs yourself)
- **No** - The local council is paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance

Which applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - the council isn't paying anything. I'm covering everything myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You've met all the eligibility requirements. Let me now provide you with the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me report your eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT**

Great news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

---

### **Summary of Your Eligibility:**

You meet all the requirements because:
- ✅ Alex is 15 years old (under 16 - automatic qualification)
- ✅ Alex is in full-time education (not working)
- ✅ Alex is not receiving benefits in their own name
- ✅ Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✅ You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✅ You live with Alex and are responsible for them
- ✅ No one else is claiming for Alex
- ✅ You are paying for Alex's accommodation and maintenance yourself

---

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide required documents:**
   - Proof of your identity
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
3. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit
4. **Payment schedule** - Payments are made every 4 weeks

For more information, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Congratulations, and best of luck with your application!
